about: What Talk says from recordings: the landing page before anybody has signed in, and the urgent-help page, which anybody can open. Spoken from pre-recorded files (public/voice/onboarding), never generated per visit. Edit the text here, then run `npm run build:voice`. English is the source. The Wolof was drafted by the model, back-translated to check the meaning, and is marked draft until a Gambian translator has checked it — correct `wo` here and set `woDraft` to false.

lines.wo: Dalal ak jàmm ci Talk Therapy.

lines.en: To begin a session with us, please sign in.
lines.wo: Ngir tàmbli ab session ak nun, bu la neexee sign in.
lines.woBack: To start a session with us, please sign in.

lines.en: You can use your email, or Google.
lines.wo: Mën nga jëfandikoo sa email, walla Google.
lines.woBack: You can use your email, or Google.

lines.en: To continue, the consultation is two hundred dalasi.
lines.wo: Ngir nu wéy, consultation bi two hundred dalasi la.
lines.woBack: For us to continue, the consultation is two hundred dalasi.

lines.en: This first consultation helps me understand what you are going through, so I can find the right person to help you.
lines.wo: Consultation bi njëkk dina ma dimbali ma xam li ngay dundu, ngir ma man la wutalaal provider bi baax te war la dimbali.
lines.woBack: The first consultation will help me understand what you are going through, so that I can find you the right provider who can help you.

lines.en: Tap Pay, then choose Wave or your card. Approve it on your phone, and come back here.
lines.wo: Bësal Pay, daldi tànn Wave walla sa card. Confirm ko ci sa phone, nga dellusi fi.
lines.woBack: Press Pay, then choose Wave or your card. Confirm it on your phone, then come back here.

lines.en: Thank you. Now, let us begin.
Welcome back. Let us carry on.
If you are in danger right now, call one-one-seven for the police, or one-one-six for an ambulance.
lines.wo: Su fekkee yaa ngi ci danger léegi, woo one-one-seven ngir police, walla one-one-six ngir ambulance.
lines.woBack: If you are in danger now, call 117 for the police, or 116 for an ambulance.

lines.en: For a fire or an accident, call one-one-eight. These calls are free.
lines.wo: Su dee lak-lak walla accident, woowalleen one-one-eight. Woté yii amuñu fay.
lines.woBack: If it is a fire or an accident, call 118. These calls are free.

lines.en: If you are under eighteen, tell an adult you trust today: a parent, a teacher, or a health worker.
lines.wo: Soo amagul eighteen, waxal tey ak mag boo wóolu: sa parent, sa teacher, walla health worker.
lines.woBack: If you are not yet eighteen, talk today to an adult you trust: your parent, your teacher, or a health worker.

lines.en: You do not have to carry this on your own. Telling one person is often the hardest step, and the most useful.
lines.wo: Doo war a yenu lii yaw rekk. Wax ko benn nit mooy li gën a jafe yenn saa yi, te moo gën a am njariñ.
lines.woBack: You should not carry this alone. Talking to someone is sometimes the hardest part, but it is the most helpful.
